bespoke_clusters.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: SMPTE theatrical motion pictures run at 24 frames per second (fps), while broadcast video uses 30 or 60 fps.
core_mechanism_bullets: SMPTE theatrical motion pictures run at 24 frames per second (fps), while broadcast video uses 30 or 60 fps.
Animating 'on twos' holds each drawing for 2 frames (12 drawings per second), halving studio ink-and-paint labor.
bespoke_clusters.worked_field_example: A 5-second character action sequence at 24 fps requires 120 total frames, or 60 unique drawings when animated on twos.
bespoke_clusters.counselor_tabletop_demo: Flip a 24-page hand-drawn flipbook at 1 second vs 2 seconds to demonstrate how frame rate governs perceived motion smoothness.

bespoke_clusters.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: 3D character rigs bind a polygonal mesh to an inverse-kinematics (IK) skeletal hierarchy using vertex weight painting.
core_mechanism_bullets: 3D character rigs bind a polygonal mesh to an inverse-kinematics (IK) skeletal hierarchy using vertex weight painting.
Stop-motion puppet armatures use locking ball-and-socket joints and tie-down bolts to eliminate camera frame jitter.
